articles.title: ‘I do a really good version of AC/DC’s Highway to Hell, which throws people’: Sharleen Spiteri’s honest playlist
articles.description: The Texas singer was fascinated by Elvis Costello as a kid and admires Nancy Sinatra’s sass and strength, but which of her own songs changed her life? The first song I fell in love with My mum gave me an old Dansette record player and a pile of albums. I must have been eight or 10, with my younger sister Corinne, getting butterflies to These Boots Are Made for Walkin’ by Nancy Sinatra. Years later, I read that she was told to sing it with a much more provocative attitude. You can hear the sass and the strength. Maybe that’s where my whole “don’t fuck with me” thing came from. articles.title: Light in the dark: 20 long books for short winter days
articles.description: Turn off your phone, get cosy and commit to some of literature’s biggest and best novels. From Don DeLillo’s Underworld to The Luminaries by Eleanor Catton, these epic reads are worth taking your time over Life starts all over again when it gets crisp in the fall,” wrote F Scott Fitzgerald in The Great Gatsby, and after the beach reads of summer, now feels like the time to settle down to more ambitious projects. Not slim works like Gatsby, but the bigger beasts you have been circling for some time. A book to wrap yourself up in as autumn becomes winter. The year I spent reading The Lord of the Rings when I was eight made me want to be a writer. The novel’s scope and the sheer amount of time I lugged it around with me combined, so that whatever I was doing, part of me was always thinking about it. This is what long books, in particular, can do. Continue reading...
